expectations.text: Uses native events: (e.target as HTMLInputElement).value, NOT e.detail.value or CustomEvent
expectations.evidence: Line 62: `const target = e.target as HTMLInputElement;` followed by `target.value` on line 63. No use of e.detail.value or CustomEvent anywhere in the output.

expectations.text: Uses wa-stack or wa-gap utility classes for vertical layout
expectations.evidence: Line 119: `<form className="wa-stack wa-gap-m"` on the form element. Also line 102: `className="wa-stack wa-gap-m wa-align-items-center"` on the success state div.

expectations.text: Has required prop on name and email inputs
expectations.evidence: Line 127: `required` on the Name Input component. Line 136: `required` on the Email Input component.

expectations.text: Uses type='email' on the email Input
expectations.evidence: Line 135: `type="email"` on the Email Input component.

expectations.text: Has loading prop on submit Button during async submission
expectations.evidence: Line 156: `loading={isSubmitting}` on the Button. isSubmitting is set true at line 86 before the async call and reset in the finally block at line 96.

expectations.text: Wraps fields in a <form> element (not just a div)
expectations.evidence: Line 118: `<form className="wa-stack wa-gap-m" onSubmit={handleSubmit} noValidate>` wraps all Input, Textarea, and Button elements, closed at line 161.

claims.evidence: Line 17: `import { Button, Input, Textarea } from '@/components/ui';` -- uses the Kigumi wrapper imports, not raw wa-* tags.
Line 93: `setFormData({ name: '', email: '', message: '' });` resets all fields after the async call resolves.

claims.claim: Button is disabled during submission to prevent double-sends
Errors clear as the user types into the affected field
claims.evidence: Lines 66-72: Inside handleInput, if the current field has an error, it is deleted from the errors state on input.

suggestions.reason: No assertion checks that the event handler parameter type is `Event` (not `React.ChangeEvent`). The native event type matters for web component compatibility -- an output could use `(e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => e.target.value` which would satisfy expectation 1 literally but use the wrong event type for wa-* components.
No assertion checks that the prerequisite `npx kigumi add` install step is present. Without it, the imports from @/components/ui would fail. This is important for a form composition skill to verify.

eval_feedback.overall: The six assertions form a solid checklist for core form patterns. The without-skill baseline passed all of them, which suggests the assertions may not be discriminating enough to justify a skill -- consider adding assertions that test for subtler web component patterns (Event vs React.ChangeEvent, data-user-invalid for WA validation styling) that a baseline model is less likely to get right.
